title: Cobalt shift log — celeste — 2026-12-20
content:
Quick context:
- Night -> morning handover. Quiet first half, then a burst of alerts around 07:12 UTC from northamerica-1 serving cluster.
- Purpose of this doc: scratchpad for actions + runbook updates I need to make before I hand off. Not polished.

Timeline (local notes, rough):
07:10 - small pager: high 99th latency for /v1/generate on model:rw-slim-2.0-quant
07:11 - alert rate increases, noise from many clients. Pager escalated.
07:14 - observed 502 errors start, spike to 1.1% of requests.
07:18 - rolled a temporary routing rule to send traffic to rw-slim-2.0-fp16 in the same pool (fallback).
07:22 - errors decreased to ~0.05%, latency returned to baseline.

What I saw (raw checks I ran):
- Prometheus queries: 
  - error rate: sum(increase(http_requests_total{job="frontend",status=~"5.."}[5m])) by (route) -> spike concentrated on /v1/generate for rw-slim-2.0-quant
  - cpu/mem: node_cpu_seconds_total and node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes show nodes in pool had CPU at ~70% and memory available dropping on a couple hosts.
- kubectl -n serving top pods (northamerica-1-pool-a): a few pods OOMKilled (killed by kernel) between 07:05 and 07:12.
- journalctl on affected nodes: repeated OOM killer messages for processes named "inference-worker" and "kv-cache-manager".
- GitHub PR referenced below: small change to kernel scheduling? (PR 891) - irrelevant, merged 2 days ago, but run on same nodes.
- Noted high number of long-running requests (context length heavy) that matched a new partner traffic pattern (X-Client: partner-verbosely)

Immediate actions taken:
- Added routing rule to route partner traffic to dedicated capacity pool (temp) — reduced cross-traffic contention. (linear INF-678 created)
- Temporarily increased memory request for inference-worker on the pool via kustomize patch -> rebooted pods gracefully (rolling restart).
- Set alert threshold back to normal once 502s fell below 0.2% for 10min.
- Opened a short postmortem note (internal) and flagged for full RCA only if we see recurrence.

Follow-ups / Runbook TODOs (high priority):
- [ ] Update runbook section "memory pressure in serving pools" to include steps I took: how to patch deployment and check OOM context. (owner: celeste) -> include exact kustomize snippet used.
- [ ] Add a monitoring panel (per-pool) for ephemeral OOMKills and per-pod RSS to console dashboard; link metric names and alert conditions. (owner: maya)
- [ ] Add partner traffic tag (X-Client header) to routing rules guide so SEs know how to carve traffic without causing broad fallback. (owner: solutions-eng)
- [ ] Create a canary config to limit context length for specific partners at edge (short-term mitigation). (owner: eng-serving-runtime)
- [ ] Follow up with infra about node oom configuration (vm.overcommit and oom_score_adj defaults) — asked @Jordan to check qemu/VM tuning.

Notes for runbook text (copy-paste bits I will insert):
- "If you observe OOMKilled processes in serving pool -> check `kubectl describe pod` for Last State: Terminated (OOMKilled). Inspect `journalctl -u kubelet` on node for cgroup kill messages. Temporarily increase `resources.requests.memory` on the deployment and perform a rolling restart with graceful termination (SIGTERM timeout = 120s). If OOM persists after 2 restarts, isolate traffic and escalate to infra. "

Open questions / unresolved:
- Why did kv-cache memory spike? Could be a cache eviction bug: the cache grew to hold partner's long contexts. Need heap dump if we can reproduce.
- Were there any recent quantization profile changes for rw-slim-2.0-quant? Check model catalog change log. If quantized runtime path changed memory layout, might cause leak.
- Is there correlation to PR #891? (low signal now; flagged for further review)

Incidents/tickets created:
- Linear INF-678: temporary routing + followup (created 2026-12-20 07:25)
- Infra ticket: VM oom tuning (INC-4321) — assigned to Jordan
- GitHub issue placeholder: runtime/kv-cache memory growth (link added to PR comments)

Useful commands I used (copy for runbook):
- kubectl -n serving get pods -o wide --selector=pool=northamerica-1-a
- kubectl -n serving describe pod <pod> | sed -n '1,80p'
- ssh node-12 && sudo journalctl -u kubelet -S "2026-12-20 06:50" | grep -i oom
- curl -v https://northamerica-1.api.redwood/v1/health (check routing)
- prometheus query examples: increase(container_memory_working_set_bytes{pod=~"inference-worker.*"}[5m])

Personal TODOs (for next 48h):
- Draft runbook text + kustomize snippet (today, celeste).
- Pair with Maya to add the dashboard panel (blocker: needs datasource mapping).
- Reproduce partner pattern in a test pool to capture heap/pprof if possible.
- Coordinate a low-risk restart of the remaining nodes in pool during maintenance window if infra recommends kernel tunings.

Handover notes for next oncall (Maya):
- Pool northamerica-1-a currently on fallback routing: rw-slim-2.0-quant -> rw-slim-2.0-fp16. Fallback expires in 6 hours unless INF-678 changed.
- Alert thresholds temporarily relaxed; if you see 5xx > 0.5% again, do steps in runbook (increase memory request + rolling restart).
- If you need to revert routing rule: run `rcli route revert --id inf-678-temp-route` (I've saved last config under /tmp/route-inf-678.json on the console).

Random miscellany (notes to self):
- Remember to ack the partner's engineering contact before I leave — they asked for a quick postmortem note.
- Save the exact kustomize patch in the runbook with the diff output from kubectl apply --dry-run=client.

Sign-off: Celeste Ramos (oncall)
07:55 UTC handover to Maya (briefed in Slack, pinned INF-678).

Appendix: raw fragments I will prune later:
- "kustomize patch: 
  - op: replace
    path: /spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/requests/memory
    value: \"8Gi\""
- short slack snippets: "Paging: 502s on /v1/generate — routing to fp16 pool while we investigate OOMs"
